Md. Toufiq Imam, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner. 
Md. Haroon-or-Rashid, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No. 7.
parties:
Abdul Aziz Biswas (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and 
co-operatives and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Jahangir Hossain, J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the order bearing Memo No. ইপ/অভন-১০/২০০/৮৪৬ dated 16-9-2009 issued under the signature of the Respondent No. 2 canceling Administrative approval to construct Dohakula Union Parishad Complex on the site/place and giving Administrative approval to construct Union Parishad Complex on the site/place mentioned in the Memo Annexure-F and why a direction should not be issued upon the respondents to cancel the same.

2. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner is a freedom fighter who has been involved in social activities in the locality. In order to make vigorous local government and to render prompt service to the people of the grassroots level, government decided to build complex in all Union Parishads across the country. For selecting site of the complex a guide line (paripattra) was provided by the government on 28-12-2005. As the Dohakula Union Parishad, Bagharpara, Jessore was included in the newly formed Pourashava, a new site was required to be selected for constructing a Union Parishad Complex. Thereafter, respondent No. 3 visited four places in the territory of the said Union Parishad for the same purpose. Out of which, Sukdebnagar was lastly proposed with a recommendation for approval on 28-6-2005 and subsequently, upon the decision of the government, respondent No. 2 approved the proposal in respect of the Sukdebnagar for construction of the Union Parishad Complex vide Memo dated 4-4-2006 and accordingly a fund was sanctioned by a memo dated 25-11-2007 amounting to Taka 42,00,000 as cost for construction of the same at Sukdebnagar. While local people were eager to see the new Union Parishad Complex on the selected site, the political scenario as well as government was changed. Thereafter, a further inquiry was held on the three sites and consequently on 29-1-2009 Additional District Magistrate recommended a new site namely "Bohorampur" which is located at the corner of the union. But the local members of the Union Parishad made a representation to the Deputy Commissioner demanding to sustain previous selected place. Despite the said objection, the Deputy Commissioner forwarded the same with a recommendation to the ministry on 9-8-2009 for approval.

3. Ignoring the will of the local people, the Respondent No. 2 through impugned memo dated 16-9-2009 cancelled the administrative approval to construct Dohakula Union Parishad Complex on the selected site and granted further approval for construction of the Union Parishad Complex on the newly selected site at Bohorampur. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid impugned order, the petitioner moved this court with a petition and obtained the present rule.

4. Respondent No. 7 has entered appearance in the rule upon filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material allegations brought by the petitioner stating inter alia that the members of the union parishad selected four places through a resolution vide No. 22 dated 29-2-1994 and Upazila Nirbahi Officer after investigation of the said four places, selected a site at Boharampur Bazar as it was convenient for the majority people of the union and the same was forwarded with a recommendation to the respondent No. 3 who proposed Sukdebnagar wherein only a primary school is situated. Whereas an old renowned hut, primary school, madrasha, post office and family welfare centre had been established at the place of Bohorampur Bazar connecting with Jessore Narail high way. Meanwhile, soliciting votes by seven members, selected site at Bohorampur Bazar while five members favoured site at Sukdebnagar. Consequently, site was selected at the place of Bohorampur by a resolution in the meeting held on 29-5-2005 by the union parishad and forwarded the same to the respondent No. 3 vide Memo No. 2005/75 dated 12-6-2005 but ignoring the will of the majority members as well as local people of the union parishad, the respondent No. 2 approved the site of the complex at Sukdebnagar. Thereafter, upon an objection, the UNO again sent a report preferring Bohorampur Bazar to the respondent No. 3 who ultimately made recommendation on Bohorampur Bazar for approval on 29-1-2009. On the basis of that recommendation respondent No. 2 approved site at Bohorampur Bazar by issuing impugned latter dated 16-9-2009. It has been further stated that the decision of respondent No. 2 is conclusive. It cannot be determined in a summary procedure under writ jurisdiction and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged.

5. Mr. Md Toufiq Imam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that following report with a recommendation of the Deputy Commissioner, the approval was given for construction of the Union Parishad Complex at Sukdebnagar. So there is no any scope to give new approval after canceling the previous one. He submits that the selected site/place namely Sukdebnagar is situated at the hub of the Union Parishad. Majority people of the Union Parishad have scope to get in touch easily with the complex as approved by the government earlier. It will be convenient if the complex is constructed at the place of Sukdebnagar, approved by the government. Drawing our attention to the case of Golam Murtaza Bhuiyan vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 47, he submits that paripattra dated 28-12-2005 for selecting site of the Complex was made after about two years of the aforesaid cited judgment. He finally submits that though the paripattra is not a law but it is the guide line of the path for the purpose of selecting site of the complex. Without following the same, no decision initially can be taken for selection of the site as well.

6. On the other hand, Mr Md Haroon-or-Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No. 7 contends that prior to the previous approval, the majority members of the union parishad selected site for constructing complex at Bohorampur Bazar and UNO also proposed the same place of being inquired. But the respondent No. 2 gave approval for the complex at Sukdebnagar ignoring report and recommendation of the local authority. He submits that having realised the same, the concerned authority rightly gave approval for constructing complex at Bohorampur Bazar after canceling the earlier approval. There is no illegality in passing the impugned Memo as the same was considered after scrutiny of the reports of the local authority and also demand of the local people. Relying upon a case of Golam Murtaza Bhuiyan vs. Government of Bangladesh reported in 48 DLR (AD) 47, he lastly submits that grievance from a government decision as to selection of site for construction of a new complex cannot be adjudicated by a summary method under writ jurisdiction. So the rule issued by this court should be discharged.

7. Heard the learned Advocates of both the parties, perused the petition and annexures thereof and affidavit-in-opposition, wherefrom it appears that a decision of the government was made to construct a complex at Sukdebnagar in the year 2006 although the members of the union parishad and the UNO after inquiry selected the site for construction of the union parishad at Bohorampur Bazar. Upon a complaint for selection of the site a further inquiry was held by the authority concerned. The inquiry committee selected the site for construction of the complex at Bohorampur Bazar and forwarded the same for obtaining approval from the ministry as well. Accordingly, Respondent No. 2 gave administrative approval in order to construct a complex at Bohorampur by issuing impugned order dated 16-9-2009 after canceling the earlier approval order dated 4-4-2006. It further appears that there is no dispute between the government and the local body in selecting the new site for construction of the complex. There is no question of malafide or arbitrariness in the decision for approval of the site selection by the Government. Grievance from a government decision as to selection of site for constructing a new union parishad complex cannot be adjudicated in a proceeding under writ jurisdiction. The contention of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 7 is appreciated by citing a case of Golam Murtaza Bhuiyan vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 48 DLR (AD) 47 wherein their Lordships observed that:—

"Grievance arising out of a Government decision as to selection of a site for construction of a new Union Parishad Office-cum-Community centre cannot be examined in a summary proceeding under the writ jurisdiction."

<u>8. On perusal of the record it reveals that the local body selected the site at Bohorampur and on inquiry the Deputy Commissioner also gave report to the approving authority as well for its approval. So there is no violation of any rule of the rules of Business. Their Lordships further opined in the said case that:</u>

<u>"Government decision to select a site for a local body on the resolution of the Union Parishad and the report of the Deputy Commissioner cannot be questioned as being in violation of the Rules of Business."</u>

<u>9. It appears further to us that with regard to selection of site for construction of the complex in the union parishad is absolute policy of the government. On which place the complex will be built, it is the duty of the government to decide.</u>

10. In this contention, a decision may be cited upon a case of Md Abdul Motaleb Sarker vs Md Laskar Ali reported in 18 BLT (AD) 311 wherein it was held that:

"It appears that the subject matter of the suit is shifting of the office of Shihara Union Parishad from its present site and the plaintiff sought for declaration that the order dated 10-4-1986 passed by the Government shifting the same to the new site is illegal, void and inoperative.

It appears that the site selection is the business of the Government and relates to policy matter concerning the administration and the petitioner as plaintiff had no locus standi to challenge such a policy decision of the Government"

<u>11. In the present case the government took the decision after observing all formalities by the local authority, therefore, there is no malafide and arbitrariness in issuing the impugned order.</u>

12. In view of the discussion as above, we do not find any substance in the rule.

13. Accordingly, the rule issued by this Court is hereby discharged without any order as to costs.

The order of stay granted earlier is recalled and vacated.

End.
